text:
pagerbot: PAGER: High auth-failure rate from 3 external IPs to /v1/auth/token — 450 failures in 6m. severity=high. paging on-call.

sarah-ops: seeing same in Grafana, spike started ~2087654280. requests originate from eu-central IPs.

mike-sre: on it, tailing auth logs now. adding quick WAF rule to block the top IP.

anya-sec: flagged correlating telemetry — small number of hits include Authorization header fragments in debug logs forwarded to our staging log bucket. possible accidental log push.

sarah-ops: wait — which bucket? staging-collector-logs-prod? that shouldn't have auth headers.

devon-backend: confirmed: a recent logging change added request headers to debug payload for /v1/internal/* in staging -> we mistakenly promoted the config to prod last deploy. I rolled back the logging change in the deploy pipeline at 2087654340.

mike-sre: WAF rule rolled at 2087654360: blocked 3 IPs. rate dropped but still seeing retries from other IP ranges.

anya-sec: priority: rotate any tokens potentially present in the leaked logs, identify impacted service accounts, and start customer impact scoping.

emma-support: do we have evidence of customer tokens in the logs? need to know for customer comms.

devon-backend: sample scrubbed lines attached below. found fragments that look like bearer tokens in three log entries. snippet: ```"Authorization":"Bearer eyJhbGci...XyZ"``` — partials only, not full tokens for all entries.

anya-sec: assume compromise until proven otherwise. plan: (1) immediate rotate affected service account keys, (2) revoke all active sessions for impacted API keys, (3) start targeted customer outreach if tokens tied to customers.

sarah-ops: mike — can you revoke sessions and issue a forced logout for token scopes used by the affected endpoints?

mike-sre: will run the session-revoke job now. Command: ```./opsctl sessions revoke --selector="endpoint:/v1/auth/token" --since=2087654200``` — started at 2087654385. ETA ~2m.

mike-sre: session-revoke finished. 12,142 sessions revoked across internal svcacct tokens and 3 customer API keys flagged as active.

devon-backend: rotating the affected service account keys (svc-auth-pipeline). New keys generated and injected to prod at 2087654430. old keys disabled.

anya-sec: blocking IP ranges more broadly for now and rate-limiting the token endpoint. applying temp fallback rule to require captcha on suspicious bursts for the next 1h.

emma-support: I need a short summary for customers whose keys were revoked — can security draft wording? we should avoid implying data exfil.

anya-sec: draft: "We identified abnormal authentication traffic and proactively revoked a small set of API keys and sessions as a precaution. We have rotated internal credentials and patched a logging config that exposed header fragments to a restricted log store. No evidence of misuse of customer data has been found to date. We will follow up with additional details if our investigation identifies impacted accounts." (fine to use this for initial outreach).

liz-legal: hold on customer-specific language — add a line about contacting us if they see unexpected behavior; avoid over-committing on investigation timeline.

sarah-ops: incident timeline so far: detection 2087654280, rollback logging change 2087654340, WAF block 2087654360, session revoke 2087654385, key rotate 2087654430.

anya-sec: next steps: forensic pull of the staging->prod deploy logs, full scan of logs in staging-collector-logs-prod for any unredacted auth data (done by sec infra), coordinate with customer ops for targeted outreach (emma), legal to review wording (liz). Assignments: devon -> deploy audit, mike -> confirmation of revocations and monitoring, anya -> log scan & root-cause, emma -> draft + queue customer comms, liz -> legal review.

devon-backend: audit in progress; I see the config promotion was an automated pipeline approval triggered by a tag. node:ci promoted build 20260312-7 to prod at 2087654279. adding guard to pipeline to prevent header->logs in prod.

mike-sre: monitoring alert rule tightened for next 24h, and dashboard pinned to incident channel. will keep rate rules on and collect 30s histograms.

anya-sec: any proof of exfil beyond the log snippets?

devon-backend: not yet. copies in the log bucket are access-controlled; only a small ops role accessed them. we are preserving snapshots for forensics.

emma-support: ready to send initial outreach to the 3 customers with revoked API keys. I'll wait for legal approval to send.

liz-legal: approved with minor edits. go ahead.

anya-sec: marking incident as active-mitigation. severity: high -> containment in place. we'll reconvene in 30m to confirm post-rotation telemetry. :hourglass_flowing_sand: 

pagerbot: INCIDENT UPDATE: status=active-mitigation; assigned=[devon-backend,mike-sre,anya-sec,emma-support]; incident_channel=#incidents; bridge=link_to_bridge; start_ts=2087654280.

sarah-ops: thanks team. please log any additional changes here so customers and execs can be briefed if needed.

mike-sre: I'll post follow-up once 1h telemetry looks clean.

anya-sec: locking down until then. great work. :shield:
